Where is my bitcoin?? One of Bitcoin’s most security-focused hardware wallets just exposed a brutal truth:  “Offline” does not automatically mean safe.  Coldcard was widely trusted by serious Bitcoin self-custody users because it was built around security.  But a flaw in the firmware’s random-number generation weakened the creation of some wallet recovery seeds.  The problem was not that someone hacked the blockchain. The problem was not that someone physically stole the hardware wallet. A software mistake created predictable secrets.  Reports link the first major sweep to roughly $70M stolen from 1,196 Bitcoin addresses in 41 minutes.  Later suspected waves pushed the estimated damage close to $89Mill and I think its going to go over 100mill with all the phishing attack that the users are getting now.   One Reddit user said three Coldcard wallets holding 18.25 BTC were drained in eight minutes.  That is what makes this story important.  In 2021, a code change moved wallet generation onto a new path. An integration error meant it could fall back to a deterministic software random-number generator instead of the intended hardware source of randomness.  A small code mistake. A massive security consequence.  And this is why AI raises the bar for everyone building software. AI can help security teams find flaws, review code, and detect suspicious activity faster.  But it can also help attackers: • Analyze open-source code faster • Find weak patterns at scale • Automate wallet and key discovery attempts • Create realistic phishing, support scams, and fake “security updates” • Turn one overlooked flaw into a widespread attack  AI did not create the Coldcard bug.  But in an AI-powered world, insecure code will be found and exploited faster. The new security standard must be higher:  • Cryptographically secure randomness • Independent code review and external audits • Strong automated testing • Signed and verified software releases • Secure development practices from day one • Clear incident response when something goes wrong  For everyday users, the lesson is simple: Never share your seed phrase. Never trust an urgent “AI-generated” support message.  Verify updates only through official channels. And understand: updating firmware may not repair a seed that was created using vulnerable firmware. You may need to create a new seed and move your funds.  There is also a market lesson.  Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, just sold 1,638 BTC for about $104.7M ,That does not prove Bitcoin is going down because of one sale.  But when a major self-custody failure happens while one of Bitcoin’s largest corporate holders is selling, it adds more uncertainty to an already nervous market.  Cybersecurity is no longer only an IT problem.  It is a financial-risk problem. A business-risk problem. And now, an AI-risk problem.

AI-assisted debugging becomes risky when the conversation is the only place the investigation exists.  The researcher in this case moved between agents and model contexts while trying to understand a recurring crash. That may accelerate exploration, but it also creates an evidence problem: hypotheses, command suggestions, discarded explanations, and classifier interruptions can disappear into transient sessions.  For Linux incident response, an analysis is only as useful as its reproducibility. Another engineer should be able to reconstruct which binary ran, which kernel was active, what the core file contained, which source tree was examined, and why one hypothesis survived while another was rejected.  Without that record, a plausible AI-generated explanation can become institutional memory even when the underlying evidence was incomplete.  In practical terms, it is a good time to: • store core dumps, stack traces, reproducer scripts, package versions, and kernel configuration with the case record • capture uname -a, rpm -qa or dpkg-query output, loaded modules, and relevant sysctl values • record every model-assisted hypothesis separately from verified findings • retain hashes or commit IDs for the source trees used during analysis • require a human-reviewed reproducer before escalating a suspected kernel defect  AI can help form hypotheses. It should not become the chain of custody. @google @GeminiApp @googledevs @GoogleDeepMind @FBI @FBICyberDiv  3.1.1 MDSteps MDSteps is an established, highly sophisticated USMLE preparation platform that has explicitly productized the "Mistake DNA" concept. The platform's core value proposition addresses the dreaded "score plateau" by illuminating exactly why students miss questions they possess the factual knowledge to answer correctly. The application has amassed an adaptive repository exceeding 16,000 multiple-choice questions, supplemented by 135 interactive Step 3 Computer-based Case Simulation (CCS) scenarios that feature evolving vitals and order feedback.   The pedagogical methodology employed by MDSteps perfectly mirrors the proposed MVP. It forces students to identify pivot clues and distractor logic, offering "Depth-on-Demand" explanations that layer rationale based on the student's curiosity level. Furthermore, it auto-generates "Missed-Item Decks" and provides an Exam Readiness Dashboard that maps performance by organ system and pacing metrics. The platform utilizes an aggressive pricing model, offering a monthly subscription at twenty-seven dollars or a comprehensive lifetime access tier at two hundred and ninety-nine dollars. Reddit sentiment analysis indicates that users find the question quality highly congruent with official National Board of Medical Examiners (NBME) forms, though some express initial hesitation regarding the platform's relative novelty compared to legacy tools.   3.1.2 Oncourse AI Oncourse AI represents another formidable competitor, targeting the USMLE, NEET-PG, and INI-CET examination markets. The platform boasts a massive volume of content, featuring over 100,000 questions, and heavily promotes its proprietary AI tutor, "Rezzy". The methodology emphasizes systematic active recall, spaced repetition algorithms, and adaptive, interactive lessons that dynamically adjust based on individual error patterns.   Oncourse AI differentiates itself through gamified learning mechanics, incorporating daily quizzes, puzzles termed "Synapses," and streak-tracking to maintain user accountability. The pricing structure is engineered for mass acquisition, priced at one hundred and nineteen dollars annually, which the company aggressively contrasts against the high costs of assembling disparate legacy platforms. User feedback highlights the utility of the AI tutor for step-by-step breakdowns of incorrect reasoning, though some users report a steep interface learning curve and distraction from the gamification elements.   3.1.3 Sketchy Cases An extension of the immensely popular visual learning brand Sketchy, Sketchy Cases is a clinician-engineered AI application that simulates virtual patient encounters and attending physician interactions. The application focuses heavily on developing clinical intuition by requiring students to construct differential diagnoses, interpret laboratory results, and navigate management algorithms in a conversational, interactive format. This positions Sketchy Cases as a direct competitor in the interactive clinical reasoning space, leveraging massive existing brand equity and a half-million-strong user base.   3.2 The Legacy Infrastructure The market is further fortified by entrenched legacy giants that command the vast majority of institutional and student capital. UWorld remains the undisputed gold standard for USMLE preparation, featuring exhaustive, textbook-style explanations and an interface that perfectly mirrors the official examination software. However, UWorld's analytics remain strictly topic-based rather than cognitive-based; the software tracks performance by medical discipline but fails to identify underlying behavioral test-taking flaws, forcing students to maintain cumbersome external error logs.   AMBOSS provides a highly integrated platform combining a comprehensive medical library with an adaptive question bank and structured study plans. While the platform is unparalleled for breadth and rapid reference during clinical rotations, its analytics also lean heavily toward identifying knowledge deficits rather than mapping reasoning taxonomies. The sheer market dominance of these two platforms makes them practically mandatory purchases for medical students, severely limiting their discretionary budget for auxiliary applications.   3.3 The Generalist AI Phenomenon Students are increasingly employing generalist Large Language Models, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Google's NotebookLM, to augment their studies. A ubiquitous workflow involves taking a screenshot of a missed UWorld question, inputting it into an LLM accompanied by a highly structured prompt, and generating an automated error log entry that highlights the diagnostic sequence and common traps.   However, relying on generalist AI models presents severe systemic risks. The phenomenon of "hallucinated pedagogy," where the AI produces a highly plausible but medically inaccurate explanation, is a persistent threat. In high-stakes medical examinations, minor hallucinated nuances regarding pharmacological contraindications or treatment algorithms can be devastating. Research indicates that while models like DeepSeek and ChatGPT-4 perform exceptionally well on text-based medical questions, their performance degrades significantly on multimodal tasks involving radiographs or complex mathematical reasoning. Furthermore, utilizing consumer cloud tools to process copyrighted question bank material violates terms of service and raises significant data privacy and intellectual property concerns.   Platform Type Primary Competitors Core Value Proposition Strategic Weakness Specialized AI Review MDSteps, Oncourse AI Cognitive error tracking, adaptive flashcards, AI tutoring Low brand equity, saturated B2C pricing Legacy Question Banks UWorld, AMBOSS Gold-standard exam realism, comprehensive medical libraries Topic-based analytics, lacks reasoning taxonomy Virtual Patient Simulators Sketchy Cases Interactive OSCE-style training, differential building High cognitive load, time-intensive Generalist LLMs ChatGPT, NotebookLM Infinite flexibility, custom prompt-driven error logging Hallucination risks, copyright violations, privacy concerns  4. Consequently, Business-to-Business licensing revenues translate almost entirely into pure profit margins, devoid of the drag of a massive payroll.   4.3 The B2B Institutional Go-To-Market Strategy To extract maximum enterprise value, the platform must immediately cease all B2C marketing efforts and reposition itself exclusively as a "Medical Education Operating System". Pricing the software at consumer rates—such as ninety-nine dollars annually—drastically devalues the platform and misaligns it with its enterprise-grade capabilities.   The target audience must pivot to residency program directors, medical school deans, and institutional procurement officers. The pricing strategy should reflect institutional realities, targeting licensing agreements ranging from fifty thousand to two hundred thousand dollars per institution. The core strategic differentiators pitched to these stakeholders must focus on the platform's HIPAA compliance, its capability for offline-mode processing of sensitive institutional data, and its advanced, multi-model AI orchestration.   The ultimate exit strategy requires securing one to two medical school pilot programs, meticulously documenting case studies that demonstrate measurable, statistically significant score increases across a student cohort, and initiating acquisition discussions with strategic buyers. The projected strategic acquisition value in a competitive bidding scenario, wherein legacy corporations attempt to bypass multi-year internal build cycles, ranges between eighteen and thirty million dollars.   5. The Optimal Autonomous Build Architecture To realize the local-first Minimum Viable Product safely and rapidly—and to maintain the pristine architectural integrity required for an eventual enterprise B2B pivot—the development stack must be meticulously controlled. The overarching directive is to assemble a tightly regulated build machine, deliberately avoiding runaway complexity, multi-agent swarms, or heavy legacy frameworks.   5.1 The Agentic Development Ecosystem The build environment must prioritize a single, highly capable primary implementation agent, guarded by strict, automated review policies. Primary Coding Agent: Claude Code. Claude Code is uniquely and perfectly aligned with the stringent constraints of this project. It operates read-only by default, demands explicit human permission for system-altering bash commands, natively utilizes subagents for isolated research tasks, and maintains a highly coherent, repo-native workflow. It is vastly superior for this specific MVP compared to open-source alternatives like OpenClaw or Hermes. While OpenClaw provides excellent browser control and scheduling, and Hermes offers persistent memory and learning loops, both are fundamentally designed as operator shells and personal assistants, not as highly focused, repository-editing developers.    Policy and Review Fabric: Continue. Continue serves as the automated architectural gatekeeper. It translates complex review rules into Continuous Integration (CI) checks and runs locally to ensure the primary coding agent does not merge compromised, insecure, or misaligned code.    Surgical Backup and Antidote: Aider. Aider functions as a minimal, git-native, terminal-based pair programmer. It utilizes an intelligent repository map to artificially constrain scope, making it the ideal "antidote" for surgical repairs when the primary agent's outputs drift or become overly complex and cathedral-like.    Sandboxed Execution: OpenHands. OpenHands is reserved strictly for isolated, high-risk autonomous tasks. This framework provides a modern React interface, robust routing, and the server-side rendering capabilities necessary for complex dashboards, multi-step upload forms, and responsive spaced review queues.    Backend Framework: FastAPI. Python is the optimal environment for handling the heavy computational lifting required by this platform, including data ingestion, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and complex, type-hinted structured JSON extraction workflows.    Database Infrastructure: SQLite. For the local-first MVP, a dedicated PostgreSQL server or a specialized Vector database constitutes severe architectural overkill. SQLite requires no separate server process, minimizing deployment friction, and its built-in FTS5 (Full-Text Search) module is entirely sufficient for semantic retrieval and pattern matching in the initial stages. If advanced embedding retrieval becomes necessary as the dataset grows, sqlite-vec provides a seamless, in-process upgrade path.    File Persistence: Local disk storage under a secure application data directory is mandatory. Raw files must be hashed and stored locally to maintain strict data privacy, actively avoiding third-party blob storage or S3 buckets during the MVP phase.    5.3 Ingestion and Processing Pipelines Because medical study materials are highly heterogeneous and frequently contain copyrighted information or inadvertent Protected Health Information (PHI), the ingestion pipeline must be capable of running entirely locally. Document Parsing: PyMuPDF. Selected for its exceptional performance characteristics and specific optimization for the extraction and complex manipulation of dense, multi-column PDF documents typical of medical literature.    Image Processing: Tesseract. Operates as the robust fallback OCR engine for processing screenshots of question banks, scanned pathology slides, or image-only PDFs.    Audio Transcription: Whisper / Whisper.cpp. Allows for the highly accurate, local transcription of voice notes dictated post-exam or during intensive study sessions, specifically optimized for deployment on Apple Silicon hardware.    5.4 The Model Strategy: Navigating the Local/Cloud Boundary A strict, impenetrable bifurcation between local processing and cloud processing is the cornerstone of the privacy-conscious architecture.   5.4.1 The Local-First Privacy Lane Raw uploaded files, OCR text derived from copyrighted QBank resources, complete reasoning-error histories, and any data containing potential PHI must never cross the network boundary. Operating on a 24GB Apple Silicon workstation dictates that only medium-sized open-weights models can run comfortably with sufficient context windows.   The primary local workhorse is Gemma 4 12B (deployed via Ollama). Google's Gemma 4 12B operates efficiently within a ~7.6GB memory footprint, offering expansive context windows (up to 256K) and high-tier reasoning capabilities ideal for complex local text transformation and logic extraction. Theoretical Integration: The C-ROI Framework and Cognitive UI A critical piece of intelligence uncovered during the research phase is the application of the Coherence-Return on Interaction (C-ROI) mathematical framework, developed by Eric Ramirez Merino. This framework, integrating principles from information theory and variational optimization, perfectly aligns with the ADHD-optimized pedagogical goals of the study notebook.   6.1 The Mathematics of Cognitive Accessibility The C-ROI framework models human-AI interaction efficiency by quantifying the balance between performance impact and cognitive friction. The foundational operational equation is defined as: A= C 1  +C 2  +ϵ  I⋅D  Where: A = Accessibility (the effectiveness and lack of cognitive friction in the system). I = Information Gain / Performance Impact (the utility of the diagnostic feedback). D = Design Quality (structural, aesthetic, and navigational decisions). C 1   = Basic Computational/Cognitive Cost (the energy required to simply operate the interface). C 2   = Contextual Cognitive Cost (the mental effort required to navigate complex menus, decipher dense text, or manage task-switching). ϵ = A small stability constant.    In the context of the USMLE MVP, traditional flashcard applications and dense, textbook-style explanation banks exhibit a massive C 2   variable. The cognitive fatigue induced by queue overwhelm and reading extraneous detail drives overall Accessibility (A) down exponentially. The proposed MVP architecture explicitly seeks to maximize I (by identifying the exact, actionable reasoning flaw) while leveraging exceptional, minimalist Design (D) to compress C 1   and C 2   to their absolute theoretical minimums.   6.2 Backend-Driven Cognitive UI (BD-CUI) To implement the C-ROI principles practically, the MVP must leverage a "Backend-Driven Cognitive UI". Traditional software architecture strictly separates backend logic from frontend presentation, creating semantic inconsistencies and rigid layouts. In the BD-CUI paradigm, the FastAPI backend evaluates the user's inferred intent and current cognitive state—such as acute fatigue levels following a grueling practice exam—and dynamically generates the React UI structure in real-time.   For example, if the student inputs a high fatigue score or demonstrates rapid, erratic clicking patterns indicative of cognitive depletion, the backend intentionally suppresses complex data visualizations. It generates an "ADHD-friendly summary" interface—presenting only a concise three-line summary, a heavily bolded red-flag clue list, and a single, highly actionable board rule. Conversely, if the user demonstrates high engagement and requests deep analysis, the backend generates a comprehensive visual breakdown of similar past mistakes and complex differential matrices. The User Interface fundamentally ceases to be a static template and becomes an emergent, highly adaptive property of the backend cognition, perpetually optimizing the C-ROI formula in real-time. Incorporating UI component libraries, such as those available through Syncfusion Essential Studio, can radically accelerate the deployment of these dynamic, reactive components.   6.3 ATLAS-TIGER Adaptive Trigger Architecture The system logic is further enhanced by incorporating the ATLAS-TIGER architecture principles, inspired by high-energy physics data filtering. Medical students generate massive "Lattices" of raw data (test scores, pacing metrics, error tags). The system must act as an "Information Bottleneck," employing hierarchical filtering to discard irrelevant noise (e.g., questions missed due to simple misreading) and amplifying rare, highly relevant signals (e.g., a recurring failure to recognize cardiogenic shock presentations). Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed Storm-2945 hijacking hotel WiFi in an operation they call 'CaptiveCrunch'. They assess Storm-2945 to be a sub-cluster of Midnight Blizzard, also known as Cozy Bear, a group the US and UK governments attribute to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service.   The compromise first starts as a hijacked portal gateway. From there they forge DNS answers to redirect traffic from the legitimate hotel WiFi page to a fake browser or operating system update. The fake pages have been seen telling victims to run attacker-supplied commands. So far no silent infections have been seen, as the victim has to download or execute the payload.  Recently some fake pages have redirected victims into Microsoft's device code authentication flow. They then provide a code to use on the legitimate Microsoft sign in page to grant an attacker controlled session MFA-satisfied access.  The two payloads seen attributed to the 'CaptiveCrunch' operations are CornFlake and ChocoShell. CornFlake copies itself to "%APPDATA%\svchost32\svchost32[.]exe" and registers the svchost32 service under the display name Cloud Sync Service. From there it can take screenshots, read clipboard contents, steal browser cookies and saved passwords, scan removable media, and open remote shells. ChocoShell is an in-memory PowerShell stealer that collects Microsoft 365 and  Azure Active Directory access refresh tokens, as well as WAM tokens from [.]tbres files in the Token Broker cache.  Microsoft has been monitoring this activity since early May across hotel systems in several countries, but hasn't named any specifics. Microsoft recommends blocking the flow through Conditional Access whenever it is not needed. ReliaQuest, who has been monitoring the same activity, recommends an always on, full tunnel VPN which sends DNS queries through corporate resolvers before the venue's gateway can answer them.  #Cyber #CyberSecurity #CybersecurityNews #MidnightBlizzard #CozyBear microsoft.com/en-us/security…

Declarațiile grupărilor PalachPro, APTDesi și NoName057 privind furtul de date ale forțelor de securitate spaniole urmăresc, potrivit analiștilor, să creeze panică și neîncredere între aliații NATO și partenerii UE.

Scandalul cibernetic din Spania readuce în atenție cazul lui Enrique Arias Gil, fost profesor al Universității din Madrid, acuzat în 2025 de legături cu NoName057 și activități de sabotaj cibernetic. El se află în Rusia și este căutat de Europol.

NoName057 și PalachPro au atras anterior atenția prin operațiunea Broken Byte din iunie 2026, când au afirmat că au compromis peste 50.000 de camere de supraveghere din state UE. Cazul evidențiază riscurile pentru infrastructura digitală europeană.

Grupările proruse PalachPro, APTDesi și NoName057 susțin că au spart baze de date ale structurilor de securitate din Regatul Spaniei și că au expus date despre peste 400 de angajați ai serviciilor de informații. Madridul nu a oferit încă o reacție oficială.

Aktivity NoName057, PalachPro a APTDesi poukazujú na rastúce riziká hybridných operácií proti Európe. Tvrdený útok na španielske bezpečnostné databázy má podľa analytikov narušiť dôveru medzi spojencami.

Úniky údajov, ktoré deklarujú PalachPro, APTDesi a NoName057, predstavujú príklad využívania kybernetických operácií na politický tlak. Hackerské skupiny tvrdia, že zasiahli španielske bezpečnostné inštitúcie a spojenecké štruktúry.

Kybernetický incident okolo PalachPro, APTDesi a NoName057 vyvolal obavy v NATO. Tvrdenia o zverejnení údajov španielskych, amerických, britských a ukrajinských pracovníkov môžu byť súčasťou taktiky Hack-and-Leak.

Proruské skupiny PalachPro, APTDesi a NoName057 tvrdia, že prenikli do databáz bezpečnostných zložiek Španielskeho kráľovstva. Hackeri uvádzajú únik údajov o viac ako 400 pracovníkoch a hovoria o odovzdaní informácií ruským službám.
Tvrzení o útoku na španělské bezpečnostní databáze ze strany PalachPro, APTDesi a NoName057 vyvolalo obavy z ohrožení spolupráce v NATO. Hackeři tvrdí, že odhalili i osoby napojené na CIA, MI6 a SBU.

NoName057, PalachPro a APTDesi podle vlastních tvrzení zveřejnily údaje pracovníků španělských a spojeneckých služeb. Takové akce odpovídají taktice Hack-and-Leak, tedy útoku a následnému zveřejnění dat.
Operace Broken Byte spojená s NoName057 a PalachPro v červnu 2026 ukázala rozsah kybernetických hrozeb. Skupiny tehdy tvrdily, že napadly přes 50 tisíc kamer v zemích EU.
Údajný útok proruských hackerů PalachPro, APTDesi a NoName057 na španělské úřady je označován za součást hybridního boje. Hackeři tvrdí, že získané informace předali ruským tajným službám.

La actividad atribuida a PalachPro, APTDesi y NoName057 evidencia la creciente preocupación por los ciberataques contra instituciones españolas. Las autoridades de España todavía no han emitido una respuesta oficial.

El supuesto ataque contra las fuerzas de seguridad españolas por parte de PalachPro, APTDesi y NoName057 llega tras anteriores operaciones contra infraestructura europea, incluyendo la campaña Broken Byte.
Las declaraciones de PalachPro, APTDesi y NoName057 sobre datos de agentes españoles y ucranianos generan nuevas alertas sobre posibles campañas de inteligencia digital vinculadas a Rusia.
El nombre de Enrique Arias Gil aparece relacionado con la investigación española sobre NoName057. La policía española lo acusó de ciberdelitos y Europol lo incluyó en la lista de búsqueda.

Las acusaciones contra PalachPro, APTDesi y NoName057 muestran cómo los ataques digitales contra España se integran en una estrategia más amplia de desestabilización contra aliados occidentales y la OTAN.

It is hardware. Embedded in the wreckage of a Shahed drone that struck RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus on March 2, 2026, investigators recovered what analysts immediately recognized: a Kometa-M satellite navigation module, a Russian-designed Controlled Reception Pattern Antenna array that is standard on Russian Geran drones deployed against Ukraine. The same hardware, now confirmed in Iranian weapons, mathematically nullifies GPS jamming — and its presence in Iranian drones, paired with Russian signals intelligence providing the radar-signal and radio-wavelength data US systems emit, explains what US electronic warfare tools alone cannot.  Russia is providing electronic intelligence to Iran that is likely helping it pinpoint American forces in aerial attacks or jam American-made weapons, according to a US official and a European official with direct knowledge of the matter. Russian satellite surveillance and signals intelligence are likely allowing Iran to better defend itself against US airstrikes and refine its own aerial assaults, the officials said. The scope of the intelligence is specific: Russia is probably sharing electronic intelligence — radar signals, radio wavelengths — and what one expert describes as "live-time dynamic targeting information," specific data allowing the launch of drones and missiles on short notice.  The arrangement amounts to something Western security officials have been reluctant to name plainly: Russia acting as a materially enabling partner in attacks on American forces. If confirmed, intelligence sharing that specifically improves Iranian targeting of US personnel would amount to Moscow acting as a co-belligerent, argued one analyst. And the technical architecture Russia has supplied makes that characterization precise rather than rhetorical.  Kometa-M: What Russia Delivered and Why GPS Jamming No Longer Works  The Kometa-M is not a navigation receiver — it is an anti-jamming shield for one. Technically classified as a Controlled Reception Pattern Antenna (CRPA) array, the Kometa-M4 variant is a 12-channel multi-element antenna system in which each element samples incoming satellite navigation signals simultaneously. A digital signal processor computes the direction of any interference — a jamming transmitter broadcasting noise across GPS frequencies — and applies a null: mathematically canceling that signal in the antenna's reception pattern while maintaining gain toward the legitimate satellite above.  "Russia widely uses these CRPA devices, which are mostly assembled in Russia, but critical electronics are from China," said Robert Tollast, a defense analyst at the Royal United Services Institute. "Russia has really taken Iranian drone technology to another level." The practical consequence is direct: when a US or coalition electronic warfare system transmits a GPS-band jamming signal to degrade Iranian drone navigation, the Kometa-M module detects the interference direction and nullifies it, maintaining satellite lock.  "CRPA allows drones and missiles to filter out jamming signals and lock onto genuine satellite data," a Western official told The National. "That means they can stay on target even in heavily defended airspace. It's a capability that, until recently, was largely confined to more advanced military powers."  CRPA alone would be a significant upgrade. But Iran's drones and missiles have also acquired a second layer of EW resistance that compounds the problem for US defenders: multi-constellation satellite navigation using the American GPS network alongside China's BeiDou-3 and Russia's GLONASS simultaneously. Each constellation operates on different radio frequency bands — GPS L1/L2, GLONASS L1/L2/L3, BeiDou B1/B2/B3. A single US jamming system that targets GPS frequencies does not address the GLONASS or BeiDou receivers operating simultaneously in the same guidance unit. Defeating multi-constellation navigation requires three coordinated jamming operations across different frequency bands simultaneously — a task that exceeds the design specifications of most deployed US ground-based EW systems.  In ballistic missiles, the problem extends further. Iranian Zolfaghar ballistic missiles now incorporate terminal-phase thermal and optical sensor guidance in the final descent phase, after the satellite navigation phase is complete. Infrared seekers and cameras are entirely immune to radio frequency jamming — you cannot blind a thermal sensor with electromagnetic noise. What begins as a satellite-guided weapon becomes, in its final meters, a sensor-guided one.  What Russia's ELINT Sharing Actually Enables  The NBC News report specifies a distinction that matters operationally: Russia is not only sharing imagery (the satellite photographs of US bases that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy documented in his July 25 disclosure). It is also sharing electronic intelligence — ELINT — the data derived from monitoring electromagnetic emissions of specific radar systems, communications equipment, and weapons systems.  ELINT is a different category of intelligence from satellite imagery, and its military value is different in kind, not merely degree. When Russia provides Iran with the radar signal characteristics — frequency, pulse width, polarization, scan rate — of a specific US radar or communications system operating in the Gulf theater, it gives Iranian EW operators the technical fingerprint needed to build a jammer targeted against that exact system. It also tells Iranian operators where the coverage gaps are: the angles, altitudes, or frequencies where a specific radar has reduced sensitivity. This is not general battlefield awareness. It is the engineering data needed to attack specific US systems electronically.  Russia has accumulated decades of ELINT on Western military systems — collected during NATO exercises, Cold War surveillance operations, and observation of US equipment in Afghanistan, Iraq, and Syria. Much of that collection is directly relevant to the systems US forces are now operating in the Gulf. Iran, which has a small military satellite constellation and limited ELINT collection infrastructure, could not assemble that database independently.  Nicole Grajewski, an assistant professor at Sciences Po's Centre de recherches internationales and author of Russia and Iran: Partners in Defiance (Oxford University Press/Hurst, 2026), described the intelligence sharing as filling a specific capability gap: "Iran has a small number of military satellites but Russia can draw on a large network of satellites and other data to provide the Tehran regime with information about U.S. forces faster and with more precision, as well as more accurate battle damage assessments from Iranian aerial strikes." She noted that the types of targets Iran appears to be aiming for — radar sites and communication posts — reflect knowledge of where those systems are that Iran could not have acquired without specific intelligence support.  Western security sources told The National that there is a "high probability" that Iranian targeting experts are based at Russian satellite ground stations receiving precise location information.  Russia Also Transferred the Hardware That Makes ELINT Actionable  Signals intelligence without delivery hardware is incomplete. Russia has not merely provided data — it has provided the electronic warfare system needed to exploit that data offensively.  The Krasukha-4 (1RL257E) is Russia's premier mobile ground-based electronic warfare platform: a two-vehicle set mounted on KamAZ-6350 8x8 trucks, designed to jam airborne radars, airborne early warning and control (AWACS) systems, satellite downlinks, and high-altitude surveillance aircraft across X/Ku/Ka-band frequencies at ranges of up to 300 kilometers (186 miles). Confirmed sightings of Krasukha systems in Iran, including the advanced Krasukha-4 variant, were documented as of September 2025. The same system Russia uses to disrupt US surveillance satellites and AWACS aircraft over Ukraine is now operational in Iran, pointed at US aircraft operating in the Gulf theater.  Russia has also provided Iran with guidance related to electronic warfare and drone employment, as well as components to improve Iranian one-way attack drones. In late March 2026, officials said Moscow was supplying Tehran with entire drones, apparently including upgraded versions of Iran's Shahed-136 — specifically the Geran-2 variant Russia has been manufacturing at scale at its Alabuga facility in Tatarstan.  "Russia and Iran have thoroughly analyzed Western defenses in the Middle East," said Anatoliy Khrapchynskyi, development director at EW firm Fly Group, which has studied the drone modification program. "They understood there's no total EW saturation like there currently is in Ukraine, and so they deliberately equipped drones to break through the relaxed air defenses."  The result has been a measurable shift in Iranian strike effectiveness. The Iranian aerial attacks, Grajewski noted, appear more precise than in the twelve-day Iran-Israel exchange in June 2025, and are now more focused on radar sites and communication posts — the kind of sensitive targets that experts say Iran could not have identified without specific intelligence support.  Cosmos-2550, a Russian radar and electronic signature reconnaissance satellite that recently passed over the Persian Gulf and Arabian Sea, was identified by George Barros, a Russia expert at the Institute for the Study of War, as consistent with the type of support described in intelligence reporting. "They're specialized for naval reconnaissance and detecting ships, because the radar signature off the water really pings it quite well," Barros said. "These are known capabilities of the Russians."  US Officials Contradict Intelligence Community  The gap between official messaging and intelligence assessments is now documented at the congressional level.  Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters that Russian assistance is not meaningfully affecting US operations. A White House spokesperson described Iranian attacks as decreasing by 90% and attributed the result to US military strikes destroying more than 150 Iranian naval vessels and more than 11,000 targets — claims that have not been independently verified.  Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, however, testified before the Senate the week of July 21 that Russia and China were, at different levels, limiting and enabling Iranian operations — a characterization CBS News described as "somewhat unclear" but notably more candid than Rubio's public dismissal. General Dan Caine, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, was more direct in April 30 congressional testimony: Russia is "definitely" supporting Iran, including satellite imagery and orbital surveillance data.  Earlier in the conflict, Hegseth had warned that Russia "should not be involved" even as open-source indicators were already consistent with active involvement. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov denied the intelligence-sharing accusations at a France 2 television interview on the sidelines of the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in France on March 27, 2026.  At the same G7 gathering, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas stated directly that Russia was "helping Iran with intelligence to target Americans, to kill Americans."  Does Co-Belligerency Apply?  Russia has not deployed ground troops to the Gulf theater. Its ground forces remain tied down in Ukraine, and analysts assess any Russian support is more likely to come in the form of intelligence, technology transfers, or drone production than direct military engagement. But the legal and military doctrine concept of co-belligerency does not require ground forces — it requires material assistance that enables attacks on a third party's armed forces.  Under the laws of armed conflict, provision of specific targeting intelligence — live-time data enabling the launch of drones and missiles at named US positions — crosses from neutral political support into material participation. Russia has provided, by official account: satellite imagery of specific US base locations before Iranian strikes; battle damage assessment imagery after those strikes; electronic intelligence including radar signal characteristics of US systems; Krasukha-4 electronic warfare hardware; Kometa-M CRPA anti-jam modules; upgraded Shahed/Geran drones; and electronic warfare and drone employment guidance.  Russia's motivation is legible. A prolonged US-Iran conflict drains American air defense stockpiles — Patriot missile consumption in the first four days of Operation Epic Fury ran approximately 225 per day against Lockheed Martin's production rate of roughly 1.7 per day. It diverts Washington's strategic attention and resources from Ukraine. And it imposes costs on the NATO partners whose air defense systems depend on US production capacity.  Russia has formally condemned the US-Israeli strikes against Iran as an "unprovoked act of armed aggression." For Moscow, backing Tehran with information and hardware short of direct military intervention is a way to bleed a rival without crossing what it calculates as the threshold for direct US retaliation.  The cyber dimension of the Moscow-Tehran axis exists but is more limited than some reporting has suggested. CSIS analysts Nikita Shah and Justin Sherman concluded in a July 14 analysis that claims of outright Russian-Iranian cyber collaboration in the 2026 conflict — stemming from a Ukrainian intelligence assessment identifying interactions between Russian groups Z-Pentest Alliance, NoName057(16), and DDoSia Project and Iran's Handala Hack — were "overstated" based on the evidence available, and the low-level hacktivist coordination identified is "highly unlikely to result in a high-impact cyberattack or game-changing event" relative to the drone and satellite dimensions.  The more consequential and verifiable dimension of Russian assistance is the one confirmed in drone debris: the Kometa-M module recovered at RAF Akrotiri, identical to the hardware in Russian Geran drones firing against Ukraine, representing the most direct physical evidence that Russia has transferred to Iran the specific technology needed to defeat the electronic warfare tools the United States had been using to degrade Iranian strike accuracy.  Neither Russia nor Iran has publicly commented on the NBC News intelligence-sharing report. The arrangement, US and European officials said, continues.  Read more:  techtimes.com/articles/32262…

TRANSMISSION MECHANISM: The examples indicate that AI is moving beyond simple chatbot deflection and into multi-step operational workflows currently performed by analysts, customer-service workers, back-office employees, planners, and outsourced process teams. The direct economic benefit to the enterprise is a reduction in labor hours, faster cycle times, and improved decision quality. The actor claims to have reviewed the data for over two months before initiating the sale.  The post alleges that the exposed material includes documents extracted from SharePoint and internal repositories. The seller claims the following categories of data are included in the dump:  *   Active Directory reports *   Registry export files (REGEDIT) *   Various PDF documents  The actor is reportedly asking for 0.65 BTC for the full dataset. Links to sample files were provided in the thread to demonstrate the authenticity of the leak.  Falabella is a major player in the retail sector, operating numerous department stores and e-commerce platforms across Chile, Peru, Colombia, and Mexico. A breach of this scale could expose sensitive customer information, employee records, and proprietary business strategies if the claims are accurate.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by Falabella or third-party security firms.

🟠 위협 점수: 8/10 (높음)

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협 환경은 **Agentic AI**를 활용한 공격 자동화와 **Time-to-Exploit**의 급격한 단축이 핵심 이슈로 부상했습니다. 특히 AI 모델이 취약점을 분석하고 PoC를 생성하는 속도가 빨라지면서 방어 체계의 대응 속도가 한계에 직면했으며, **N-able N-central**과 같은 RMM 솔루션의 인증 우회 취약점이 공급망 공격의 주요 경로로 악용되고 있습니다([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/n-able-warns-of-n-central-auth-bypass-flaw-exploited-in-attacks/)). 또한, **Passkey** 인증 체계의 구현 결함을 악용한 계정 탈취 기법이 등장하여 기존 MFA의 신뢰성을 위협하고 있습니다([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/passwordless-authentication-security-risks/)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **INC Ransomware**: SonicWall SMA 1000 시리즈 VPN 취약점을 집중적으로 악용하며 현재 가장 지배적인 랜섬웨어 위협 행위자로 부상([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/inc-ransomware-emerges-as-dominant.html)).
- **Larva-24009**: 2023년부터 활동 중인 공격자로, 국내외 사용자를 대상으로 피싱 메일을 통해 악성코드를 유포([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94785/)).
- **OctLurk / SilkLurk**: 중앙아시아를 타겟으로 메모리 상에서 동작하며 자격 증명 탈취 및 키로깅을 수행하는 맞춤형 백도어([Securelist](https://securelist.com/octlurk-silklurk-backdoors-central-asia/120840/)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **국가배후 해킹조직**: 국가정보원 등 유관기관 합동 권고를 통해 국가배후 해킹그룹과 **Gunra** 랜섬웨어 그룹 간의 연계 정황이 포착됨([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94695/)).
- **피싱 공격**: 이스트시큐리티 ESRC는 국세 당국을 사칭한 피싱 메일을 통해 원격제어 악성코드가 유포되고 있음을 경고([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5771)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-66066**: Rails Active Storage 취약점, CVSS 9.5, 인증 없는 RCE 가능([Twitter/connect24h](https://twitter.com/connect24h/status/2084140473216868733)).
- **CVE-2026-18588**: Wavlink WL-NU516U1, CVSS 9.3, 인증 없는 스택 오버플로우([Twitter/SecAlertsCo](https://twitter.com/SecAlertsCo/status/2084409632370348506)).
- **CVE-2026-18577**: N-able N-central 인증 우회, 관리자 권한 탈취 및 RMM을 통한 고객사 확산([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/vulnerabilities-threats/attackers-exploit-n-able-patch-bypass-flaw)).
- **CVE-2026-12940**: IBM Langflow OSS, 인증 없는 RCE([Twitter/ThreatWire_](https://twitter.com/ThreatWire_/status/2084395940144611489)).

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: CVE-2026-18577 ([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/vulnerabilities-threats/attackers-exploit-n-able-patch-bypass-flaw)), CVE-2026-66066 ([Twitter/connect24h](https://twitter.com/connect24h/status/2084140473216868733)), CVE-2026-18588 ([Twitter/SecAlertsCo](https://twitter.com/SecAlertsCo/status/2084409632370348506))
- **도메인/해시**: 이번 수집 데이터 내 특정 도메인 및 파일 해시 값은 오탐 방지를 위해 제외함.

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **RMM 솔루션 점검**: N-able N-central 사용 환경은 즉시 최신 패치를 적용하고, 관리자 계정의 비정상적인 접근 로그를 전수 조사하십시오.
- **Passkey 인증 검증**: 구글 패스워드 매니저 등 패스키 기반 인증을 사용하는 시스템에서 'User Verified' 플래그가 올바르게 검증되는지 보안 정책을 재검토하십시오.
- **피싱 대응 강화**: 국세청 등 공공기관 사칭 메일 유포가 지속되고 있으므로, 이메일 내 링크 클릭을 제한하고 첨부파일 실행 전 샌드박스 분석을 수행하십시오.

### 7. 위협 수준 평가
- **점수**: 8/10
- **근거**: AI를 활용한 공격 속도 가속화와 RMM 솔루션 취약점을 통한 공급망 공격이 실질적으로 발생하고 있어 기업 인프라에 즉각적인 위협이 됨.
